P: Serve the mains when the group sits down to Sunday dinner with Duck's family.
S: the amateur night talent show where it starts
Wings dried overnight, baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in a honey and hot sauce glaze.
the long bus rides between shows

Brown sugar, butter and cream boiled to soft ball, pecans stirred through, spooned onto paper and left to set into fudgy Southern pralines. Line two trays with baking paper. In a heavy pan, stir 200g brown sugar, 100g caster sugar, 125ml cream and 50g butter over medium heat until dissolved. Boil without stirring until it reaches 115C on a sugar thermometer. Take off the heat, add 1 tsp vanilla, a pinch of salt and 200g pecans and beat for 2 minutes until it thickens. Spoon quickly onto the trays and leave to set for 30 minutes.
Eggs boiled 10 minutes, yolks whipped with mayo, mustard, sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce, piped back, paprika on top.
M: Sunday fried chicken with ham hock greens

Chicken pieces brined in buttermilk, dredged twice in seasoned flour and fried crisp, with greens braised slowly with smoked ham hock and a splash of vinegar. Soak 1.5kg chicken pieces overnight in 500ml buttermilk with salt and hot sauce. Simmer a smoked ham hock in 1L water for 1 hour, add 2 bunches shredded silverbeet and a splash of vinegar and cook 20 minutes. Season 300g flour with paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Dredge the chicken, dip back in buttermilk, dredge again and fry at 165C for 12 to 14 minutes until 74C at the bone.
the dish on every family table
Macaroni boiled 2 minutes short, mixed with sharp cheddar and a custard of eggs, evaporated milk and butter, more cheese on top, baked at 180C for 40 minutes.
W: Dense buttery lemon pound cake baked low and slow, with a sharp lemon glaze soaked into the warm top and a spoon of whipped cream. Beat 250g soft butter and 250g caster sugar until pale. Add 4 eggs one at a time with the zest of 2 lemons, then fold in 250g plain flour and 1 tsp baking powder. Spoon into a lined loaf tin and bake at 160C for 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Mix 120g icing sugar with 3 tbsp lemon juice and pour over the warm cake. Serve slices with whipped cream.
K: Fresh lime juice and cherry syrup topped with lemonade over crushed ice with a cherry.

s.note: the amateur night talent show where it starts
s.how: Leave 1kg chicken wings uncovered in the fridge overnight, then toss with garlic powder and salt. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 50g butter with 3 tbsp honey and a good splash of hot sauce and toss the wings through until glossy.

Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and whip the yolks with mayonnaise, yellow mustard, a spoon of sweet relish and a dash of hot sauce. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Keep chilled until the show starts.

m.note: the dish on every family table
m.how: Boil 500g macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet says and drain. Whisk 2 eggs with a can of evaporated milk, 60g melted butter and a teaspoon of mustard powder. Mix with the pasta and 300g grated cheddar, top with more cheese and bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

w.how: Beat 250g soft butter and 250g caster sugar until pale. Add 4 eggs one at a time with the zest of 2 lemons, then fold in 250g plain flour and 1 tsp baking powder. Spoon into a lined loaf tin and bake at 160C for 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Mix 120g icing sugar with 3 tbsp lemon juice and pour over the warm cake. Serve slices with whipped cream.

d.how: Fill 4 glasses with crushed ice. Add the juice of half a lime and 2 tbsp maraschino cherry syrup to each, top with 200ml lemonade and add a cherry.
